candidates.exact_span: The facility discharges into Corral Canyon, thence into Tijeras Canyon in segment number 20.6.4.105 of the Rio Grande Basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Receiving-water segment identification determines which state WQS segment and criteria are used to derive or screen water quality-based effluent limits; a different segment assignment could change which numeric limits are applicable to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses for intermittent stream, designated as segment number 20.6.4.98, are wildlife habitat, livestock watering, marginal warmwater aquatic life, and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Designated uses drive selection of applicable narrative and numerical water quality criteria; interpreting which use designations govern the receiving water could change which enforceable limits are derived or deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: EPA was unable to approve section 20.6.4.98 of the NMWQS because the State did not submit a Use Attainable Assessment (UAA) to support an aquatic life designation that does not meet the CWA §101(a)(2) objective as required by 40 CFR 131.10(j)(1).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether interim segment standards are federally approvable or superseded affects which criteria may be enforced as numeric limits and how missing or non-numeric evidence for aquatic-life-related parameters should be classified when compliance cannot be directly compared.

candidates.exact_span: Prior to submittal of UAA, the designated uses of the downstream perennial stream are applicable to the receiving water. Therefore, chronic aquatic life criteria are appropriate for RP screening.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This interim rule substitutes downstream perennial-stream uses and chronic aquatic life criteria for RP screening; different readings of when the UAA trigger applies, what 'downstream perennial stream' means, or what 'RP screening' requires could change which WQBEL are imposed (A), whether additional reasonable-potential monitoring or studies are obligated (B), and how to treat periods without numeric results tied to aquatic-life criteria (C).

candidates.computation_change_reason: This is the operative gate for imposing water quality-based limits beyond technology-based effluent guidelines; whether a parameter's state WQS is 'more stringent' determines if an enforceable numeric limit must be included and compared to measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The previous permit established limits for total aluminum and total copper. These limits will be maintained.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Directly states that total aluminum and total copper numeric limits carry forward; interpretation of 'maintained' (same values, same parameters, same enforceability) determines which measurement/limit pairs are evaluated and how absent Al/Cu results are categorized relative to known obligations.

candidates.exact_span: In accordance with 40 CFR 122.45(c), total recoverable metal concentration must be established as effluent limitations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the measurement basis (total recoverable) for metal effluent limitations; comparing reported dissolved, total, or other speciation results to limits would change exceedance determinations and whether available evidence is adequate for compliance comparison.
